title: Undo Editor

examples.explanation: The undo removes "bc", the most recent typing.
The second undo has nothing left to undo, so it does nothing.

constraints: each command is "undo" or "type " followed by at least one character

approaches.name: stack of typed pieces, joined at the end
store a full copy of the text after every command

steps.title: Clarify the input
steps.description: Asks what undo does with nothing to undo, and whether typed text can contain spaces.
look_for: asks about undo on an empty history
asks about spaces in typed text
hints: Before you start, is there anything about the commands you'd want to confirm?
What should 'undo' do if nothing has been typed, and can the typed text include spaces?
Settle the empty-undo case and spaces in text before writing the parser.

steps.title: Parse each command
steps.description: Separates 'type' from the text without breaking text that contains spaces.
look_for: splits only once or slices off the 'type ' prefix
hints: Look at how you pull the text out of a type command.
What does your parsing do with 'type hello world'?
Take everything after the first 'type ' as the text, instead of splitting on every space.

steps.title: Remember each typing as a unit
steps.description: Pushes each typed piece onto a stack so an undo can remove exactly that piece.
look_for: uses a list as a stack
pushes the whole piece, not single characters
hints: Look at what an undo needs to know to do its job.
If 'bc' was typed in one command, how much should one undo remove?
Keep a stack of typed pieces; undo pops the most recent piece.

steps.title: Make undo safe
steps.description: Ignores an undo when the stack is empty instead of crashing.
hints: Try your code with an undo as the very first command.
What happens when you pop from an empty list in Python?
Only pop when the stack has something in it.

steps.title: Build the text once
steps.description: Joins the pieces at the end rather than rebuilding the string on every command.
look_for: joins the stack at the end
avoids copying the whole string on each command
hints: Look at how often your code rebuilds the full text.
Do you need the full text after every command, or only at the end?
Join the stack of pieces once, at the end.

common_mistakes.description: splits each command on every space
common_mistakes.symptom: loses everything after the first word, like 'type hello world'
crashes with IndexError on a leading undo
leaves 'b' behind after typing 'bc' and undoing

wrap_up_questions: What are the time and space complexity?
How would you add a 'redo' command that brings back the last undone piece?

origin_note: Original. Pattern: stack of typed pieces, joined at the end.
